summary: Recorded the corrected condition now that the decoupling case has a receipt. CheckRun 7b535abd3cd24baa927f2ac8f7d8d597 (exit 0) evaluated its comparison and it holds: at the same 1000 ms tick period where the shift was reproduced three times, but with every node's flush-batch tick timeout reduced from a hundred ticks to two, the fresh call returned index 4 with entry 33 at index 4, the entry at the returned index was the caller's own, and the origin's decided values were 11,12,22,33,34,35 with `decided_after_resync` 3 — its earlier buffered entries survived the re-synchronisation instead of being discarded. So the tick period alone does not produce the shift; the pairing with the earlier receipts shows the condition involves the follower's flush deadline, which the flush-deferral trace identified and which decides whether the new leader can decide its single entry during the run. I corrected the knowledge entry's conditions (revision 6) to state that and rewrote the interpretation's account, separating what stands — the caller-visible violation under the original configuration, reproduced three times at 1000 ms and once at 500 ms, with 100 and 250 ms correct — from what is withdrawn (a tick-period band as the condition). The discriminator now names the missing cell that would settle the necessary factor: a small tick with a fast flush, alongside the still-unobserved case where the origin's entries are discarded while its decided index carries progress. No execution was requested this turn (validation reports execution_requested false).
